title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over because their KU alumni license plate, number 7007, matched a stolen GMC pickup's temporary Kansas tag. In Colwich, a Flock camera alerted police to a possible stolen vehicle, but officers recognized the van and found the plate type had been entered incorrectly. A month later in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock camera led police to stop them at gunpoint and handcuff Matthew before the mistake was resolved. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs and duplicates numbers across plate types. Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate backgrounds.

Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter said Flock alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but officers must act if a stolen tag is confirmed, even when the plate type was entered wrong. Wichita police have discussed training Flock to recognize plate backgrounds. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit, non duplicated plate numbers as a fix. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops, and they hope to keep their 14 year old plate.
